sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year, from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $216 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
FY2023 was the trough: gross margin fell 8.0pp to 56.9% on $2.17 billion of inventory provisions [D298][F27][P35].
Revenue then grew 125.9% in FY2024, as Data Center revenue rose 217% on strong demand for AI computing [D338][P25].
Revenue grew 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026, driven by data center compute and networking platforms [D393][D448][P16][P10].
Data Center revenue was $194 billion, 89.7% of FY2026 revenue; product members overlap, so I use this line only and do not add members together [S56][D620].
It contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% revenue growth, with Data Center computing up 59% on Blackwell and networking up 142% on NVLink [D622][D448][P8].
Profit grew slower than revenue in FY2026: operating income rose 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, for an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
In FY2026 diluted EPS grew 66.7% against net income growth of 64.7%, as diluted shares fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Diluted share jumps of 303.7% in FY2022 and 894.5% in FY2025 look like unadjusted stock splits, so multi-year EPS CAGRs are not comparable [D251][D415].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 is well above the 32.8% window median and 2.0pp below the 62.4% high [F50][D813][D812].
Cost of revenue took 3.9pp off FY2026 operating margin, with a $4.5 billion H20 inventory and purchase-obligation charge in the first quarter [D477][P7].
R&D and SG&A leverage added back 1.3pp and 0.6pp in FY2026 [D478][D479].
In FY2024, the largest move, margin rose 38.5pp: cost of revenue added 15.8pp, R&D 13.0pp, SG&A 4.7pp and other lines 5.0pp [D353][D367][D368][D369][D370].
Net margin of 55.6% trails operating margin of 60.4% as the tax rate rose to 15.1% on fewer tax benefits [F70][F50][D434][P2].
Operating cash flow of $103 billion was 0.86x net income and free cash flow of $96.7 billion was 0.81x, the window low [F100][D435][F110][D436][D826].
Free cash flow margin of 44.8% sits near the 44.4% window median, while free cash flow to net income trails the 1.16x semis peer median [D432][D822][D436][D847].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, while inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%; the cited filings do not explain those moves [F105][D431][D437][D474][D473].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion in FY2026 from $34.7 billion, but FY2026 cash and investments of $10.6 billion equal cash alone [D441][D386][D439][F150].
FY2026 short-term investments are missing from the pack, so I draw no conclusion from that drop or the 83rd-percentile net cash rank among six peers [D844].
Investing outflow of $52.2 billion rose on higher purchases of equity investment securities and a Groq license agreement [F120][P1].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion plus dividends took 42.5% of free cash flow, and diluted shares fell 1.2% [X150][D444][D470].
Data quality: missing FY2026 short-term investments leave cash and investments at $10.6 billion and net cash at $2.14 billion, probably understated [D439][D441].
Concentration: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14%, mostly in Compute & Networking [P6].
China (including Hong Kong) revenue fell 21.4% to $19.7 billion, 9.1% of revenue, and the cited filings do not state why [D545][S24][D544].
Inventory rose 112.3% to $21.4 billion, with days inventory at 125 against 113 in FY2025, after the $4.5 billion H20 charge [D474][X222][D446][D391][P7].
Operating margin below the FY2026 level of 60.4% in the FY2027 10-K would extend the cost-of-revenue squeeze; holding above it would reverse that [F50][D477].
Days inventory above 125 days in the FY2027 10-K would extend the build; a return toward FY2025's 113 days would reverse it [D446][D391].
China revenue below $19.7 billion, or a direct customer above 22% of revenue, in the FY2027 10-K would deepen the exposure flags [S24][P6].
